_meta.by: Claude Opus 5.5 in the build session, standing in for the tier-2 model
_meta.inputs: research signals (fact ids) + promise ledger only — no outside knowledge
_meta.note: Every point cites ids the app can link to. Dixon's first bear point was corrected after reading the Q1 FY27 results filing: the earlier draft attributed Q1's profit to a fair-value gain.

bull.point: Revenue compounded ~50% a year for five years while suppliers fund working capital (−3 days).
Hits the numbers it controls: capex and telecom revenue landed on guidance; IT hardware and FY27 revenue are tracking ahead.
Profits turn into cash — operating cash is 121% of six-year profit — on a light balance sheet (D/E 0.21), with a clean auditor's conclusion.

bear.point: Q1 profit leaned on ₹528 cr of other income, and the auditor flags ₹1,110 cr of PLI income still awaiting government sign-off.
Dates and volumes are unreliable: 0 of 4 capacity dates kept and FY26 phone volumes missed by 18%.
Margin keeps sliding (4.5% → 3.8%, Q1 at 3.0%) while the promised expansion moves out to FY28.

bull.point: A cash machine: free cash flow ≈96% of profit over six years, 81% paid out, debt/equity 0.11.
Did what it said on AI and orders: AI revenue $1.8 bn → $3 bn+ annualised in three quarters; FY26 order book beat the $38–39 bn it guided.
Manufacturing turned in Q2 exactly as guided (+3.1% QoQ in constant currency).

bear.point: Growth has slowed to +4.6% last year from a 10% five-year pace, and operating margin is down 130 bps.
July's 'exit FY27 at 25%+' margin target was gone by October, with Q2 stuck at 24%.
Debtor days up from 67 to 93 and fixed assets +38% in a year — the asset-light model is getting heavier.

bull.point: Revenue ~51% CAGR over five years with operating margin up from 4.4% to 18.7%.
Growth pays for itself: negative working capital and operating cash at 133% of six-year profit.
Moderate leverage (D/E 0.37) leaves room to keep opening stores.

bear.point: Growth has more than halved to +17% last year, yet the stock trades at 80.7× earnings.
New stores weigh on returns: depreciation +52%, fixed assets +42%, ROCE off its 31% peak.
No earnings calls, so management's forward claims can't be checked against delivery.
